description: coral-agents/seller-agent/src/telemetry.test.ts's 'canonicalMessage (regression guard vs apps/landing telemetry-verify.js field order)' test (lines 71-80) never imports or references the real file (apps/landing/netlify/functions/_lib/telemetry-verify.js or telemetry-schema.js) at all -- it only asserts that canonicalMessage's own output contains a key list hardcoded a SECOND time inside the same test file. It is tautological: it will keep passing even if the two codebases' field sets diverge, providing zero actual regression protection against the real endpoint. Separately, telemetry.ts's own comment (lines 45-46: 'the two codebases must agree byte-for-byte on what gets signed, or the real verifier 401s') is factually inaccurate: apps/landing/netlify/functions/_lib/telemetry-verify.js (lines 27-51) verifies the ed25519 signature against the raw `message` bytes exactly as sent -- it never recomputes/re-serializes canonicalMessage server-side for comparison -- and only additionally schema-validates the parsed payload via telemetry-schema.js's validate(). Byte-for-byte agreement with the reference canonicalMessage implementation is not actually required for acceptance; only passing the hand-rolled schema (field types/ranges in telemetry-schema.js) is. The comment overstates a coupling that doesn't exist while the ACTUAL requirement (schema conformance) is undocumented in telemetry.ts.
